record.paper_title: Distinct Distances: Open Problems and Current Bounds
record.original_question: Let D_lines(m,n) be the minimum number of distinct distances between m points on one line and n points on another line in R^2, under the assumption that the two lines are neither parallel nor orthogonal. Determine the asymptotic order of D_lines(m,n).

evidence.quote: is Dlines(m, n ) = Ω(min{n2/ 3m2/ 3, m 2, n 2}). The ﬁrst term in the minimum is the interesting one — the other two dominate only when one point set is signiﬁcantly la rger than the other. Elekes [15] observed the upper bound Dlines(n, n ) = O(n2/ √ log n). Problem 16. Find the asymptotic value of Dlines(m, n ). Among other reasons, Problem 16 is considered interesting s ince it has many general- izations, including to problems that do not involve distanc es (for example, see [16, 45]). artifact.self_contained_problem: For positive integers $m,n$, let $D_{\text{lines}}(m,n)$ denote the minimum, over all configurations consisting of a set $P_1$ of $m$ points lying on a line $\ell_1\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ and a set $P_2$ of $n$ points lying on a line $\ell_2\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ such that $\ell_1$ and $\ell_2$ are neither parallel nor orthogonal, of the number of distinct values taken by the Euclidean distance $\|p_1-p_2\|$ as $(p_1,p_2)$ ranges over $P_1\times P_2$. Determine the asymptotic order of growth of $D_{\text{lines}}(m,n)$ as $m,n\to\infty$. In particular, in the balanced case $m=n$, close the gap between the known lower bound $D_{\text{lines}}(n,n)=\Omega(n^{4/3})$ and the known upper bound $D_{\text{lines}}(n,n)=O(n^2/\sqrt{\log n})$.
artifact.status_search_result: The best known lower bound is $\Omega(\min\{m^{2/3}n^{2/3}, m^2, n^2\})$ due to Sharir, Sheffer, and Solymosi (2013), giving $\Omega(n^{4/3})$ in the balanced case, while the best known upper bound is $O(n^2/\sqrt{\log n})$ from Elekes. The gap between these bounds remains, and the problem is treated as open in subsequent work (e.g., Natarajan–Sheffer 2025 on Pfaffian curves), with no result determining the asymptotic order.

status_evidence.title: Distinct distances on two lines
status_evidence.snippet: The number of distinct distances determined by P1×P2 is Ω(min{|P1|^(2/3)|P2|^(2/3),|P1|^2,|P2|^2}); for |P1|=|P2|=m this gives Ω(m^(4/3)), improving Elekes' Ω(m^(5/4)).
status_evidence.claim: Best known lower bound for D_lines(m,n) matches Ω(m^{2/3} n^{2/3}) in the non-degenerate range.

status_evidence.title: Distinct Distances on Pfaffian Curves
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2025) work treats distinct distances on curves and references the two-lines bound as the current state of the art, without resolving the gap with the O(n^2/sqrt(log n)) upper bound.
status_evidence.claim: The asymptotic order of D_lines(m,n) is still not determined as of 2025.
